featured.title: Sam Altman · OpenAI CEO
featured.summaryEn: OpenAI shipped three flavors of GPT-5.6 this week — Sol, Terra, and Luna. Altman's framing is unambiguous: Sol is the enterprise answer, and the pitch isn't benchmarks but dollars-per-task. He explicitly says they heard enterprises on AI cost concerns, and 5.6 Sol is a big step forward on cost-per-task, as are Terra and Luna. He separately reassured that Codex is the core of their new work product and "is not going anywhere," addressing speculation about Codex being sidelined. A third post thanked Fidji Simo on he…
featured.insightZh: OpenAI 这周一口气放了 GPT-5.6 的三个版本——Sol、Terra、Luna。Altman 的定位很清楚：Sol 是给企业的答案，重点不是刷分而是「每个任务花多少钱」。他直说听到了企业对 AI 成本的顾虑，5.6 Sol 在「dollars-per-task」上是一大步，Terra 和 Luna 也是。同时他单独发帖强调 Codex 是这套新工作产品的核心、「哪儿都不会去」——回应外界对 Codex 是否会被边缘化的猜测。另有一条是为 Fidji Simo 离开 OpenAI 表达感谢与祝福。

featured.title: Thibault Sottiaux · OpenAI（Codex & ChatGPT）
featured.summaryEn: Alongside the GPT-5.6 Sol launch, Sottiaux announced OpenAI will reset rate limits twice across ChatGPT Work and Codex over 24 hours, encouraging users to try ambitious tasks and get the hang of the new model. It's a classic launch-day move — remove friction to trial, capture mindshare. The two posts were the heads-up and the go-live confirmation.
featured.insightZh: 配合 GPT-5.6 Sol 发布，Sottiaux 宣布未来 24 小时内会把 ChatGPT Work 和 Codex 的速率限制连续重置两次，鼓励用户放手去试更有野心的任务、熟悉新模型。这种「发布即送额度」的打法很典型——降低尝试门槛、抢用户心智。两条帖子分别是预告和正式生效通知。

featured.title: Ep 90: AI 先驱 Jürgen Schmidhuber 谈 AI 现状
featured.summaryEn: Schmidhuber is wildly optimistic on AI technology but deeply pessimistic on the model companies, and expects a stock-market crash (not a civilizational one) as a renormalization of overpriced firms with little to offer. True AGI, he argues, must leave the screen for the physical world — and robot hardware is still vastly inferior to the human body, possibly decades away. Jürgen Schmidhuber — called "the father of AI" by the NYT and Forbes, author of foundational work like LSTM — delivers a strikingly contrarian "bullish on the tech, bearish on the labs" thesis. His sharpest argument is on the CapEx bubble: compute gets ~10x cheaper every five years, so companies spending a trillion on GPUs today will see that hardware worth a tenth in five years — no business model recoups that $900B loss. Nimble software companies are being forced to become utilities, investing in nuclear plants and ga…
featured.insightZh: Schmidhuber 认为 AI 技术本身前景极其乐观，但当下上千亿美元的算力狂潮是巨大的错配、股市崩盘将至；真正的 AGI 必须走出屏幕进入物理世界，而机器人硬件仍远逊于人体，可能还要几十年。 Jürgen Schmidhuber——被《纽约时报》《福布斯》称为「AI 之父」、LSTM 等奠基性工作的作者——在这期节目里给出了一套「技术极度乐观、模型公司极度悲观」的判断，非常反主流也非常值得咀嚼。 关于算力泡沫，他的逻辑最狠：算力每五年便宜约 10 倍，所以今天砸一千亿美元买 GPU 建数据中心的公司，五年内这些硬件价值会缩水到剩十分之一——没有任何商业模式能收回这 900 亿的损失。这些原本轻盈的软件公司如今被迫变成电力公司、投核电站和燃气轮机，自由现金流从千亿级掉到百亿甚至负值。加上开源模型总是几个月内追平闭源、把定价权摁死，他判断一场「重新校准」式的股市崩盘会来——不是文明崩溃，而是对「一堆估值奇高却拿不出真东西的公司」的清算。 关于 AGI 的路径，他的核心洞察是「人工科学家」：今天的大模型全是人类偏见的产物（只在人类觉得有趣的数据上训练），而真正的智能应该像婴儿一样通过自己的行动、自己发明的实验去生成训练数据——这就是他 1990 年提出的「人工好奇心」。他还认为递归自我改进（RSI）不会成为任何公司的护城河，因为核心算法都出自小型学术实验室、人人用同一锅水。至于 AI 安全，他明显比同行乐观：他从不签那些「禁止某类自我改进」的联名信，理由是「对齐」这件事本身就假设有人能决定对齐到谁的价值观，而一屋子人就有一屋子的分歧。他类比养孩子——给它们自设目标的自由才能真正变聪明，代价是不可预测，但可以像教育孩子一样引导。

items.title: Aaron Levie · Box CEO
items.summaryEn: Levie brought the enterprise-eval lens to GPT-5.6. Box ran the whole model family through its AI Complex Work eval — extremely hard tasks over enterprise document sets with the Box AI Agent — and found Sol a big step up from GPT-5.5, especially on complex, data-oriented tasks. It's a valuable third-party enterprise read rather than a vendor benchmark, useful for judging whether 5.6 is worth the upgrade.
items.insightZh: Levie 把 GPT-5.6 放到了实测视角。Box 用自家「AI Complex Work」评测集（拿企业文档集跑极难任务）评估整个模型家族，结论是 Sol 相比 GPT-5.5 有明显跃升，尤其在复杂、数据密集的任务上。这是难得的第三方企业级 eval 视角——不是官方跑分，而是真实企业场景下的能力对比，对判断 5.6 到底值不值得升级很有参考价值。

items.title: Guillermo Rauch · Vercel CEO
items.summaryEn: Rauch flagged this as "model release week," predicting Meta Spark 1.1, Grok 4.5, and GLM 5.2 will meaningfully shift token market share — because most agentic tasks need reasonably high intelligence at fast speeds, exactly where these land. He also teased that open models are about to get exorbitantly fast. The subtext: the landscape is going multipolar fast and the single-model-monopoly narrative is collapsing — which conveniently supports his pitch for Vercel's AI Gateway as a routing layer over many models.
items.insightZh: Rauch 提醒这是「模型发布周」——他预判 Meta Spark 1.1、Grok 4.5、GLM 5.2 会明显抢走 token 市场份额，理由是大多数 agent 任务需要「够聪明 + 够快」，而这些新模型正好卡这个点。他还预告开源模型即将变得「极快」。潜台词是竞争格局在加速多极化，单一模型垄断的叙事正在瓦解——这也呼应了他推销 Vercel AI Gateway（一层之上多模型路由）的商业逻辑。

items.title: Amjad Masad · Replit CEO
items.summaryEn: Masad had two things worth reading this week. On market structure: just six months ago VCs suffered "Anthropic psychosis" and convinced themselves it would be a monopoly; now the LLM market is intensely dynamic — great models keep coming from many players, including new entrants. On a deeper technical note: as AI makes coding less rigid, teams are making the runtime more rigid — he's seeing infra teams write formal specs for the first time, building more deterministic, resilient systems. His counterintuitive but s…
items.insightZh: Masad 这周有两个值得看的观察。一是市场结构：他说仅仅 6 个月前 VC 还陷在「Anthropic psychosis」里、笃定它会成垄断，现在 LLM 市场已经极其动态化——好模型会持续出现，但不止一家，包括新入局者。二是更深的技术洞察：AI 让写代码变得不那么死板的同时，团队反而在把运行时（runtime）做得更严格——他观察到基础设施团队第一次开始写形式化 spec、做更确定性的系统。他的结论很反直觉但站得住：你想跑得越快，脚下的地基就得越实。

items.title: Peter Yang · AI 教程创作者
items.summaryEn: Peter Yang offered praise with a critical edge for OpenAI. The core point: more than any other lab, OpenAI has the opportunity to make working with agents mainstream — ChatGPT with images, live voice, browser/computer use, and plugins for your favorite apps is the closest thing yet to working with a real assistant. What's notable is the distribution logic — it's not about raw model strength but about who can embed agents into ordinary people's daily workflows.
items.insightZh: Peter Yang 给了 OpenAI 一段带批评的褒奖。核心观点：比任何其他实验室都更有机会把「和 agent 一起工作」变成主流的就是 OpenAI——ChatGPT 有图像、实时语音、浏览器/电脑操作、以及接入你常用 app 的插件，这已经是最接近「和一个真正的助理协作」的形态。这个判断值得注意的是它的分发逻辑——不在于模型多强，而在于谁能把 agent 塞进普通人的日常工作流。

items.title: Nikunj Kothari · fpv Ventures 合伙人
items.summaryEn: Kothari's viral "explaining this week's model releases to my wife" bit nailed the GPT-5.6 trio: Sol is the smart one that had to clear government safety evals before release — "like getting paroled"; Luna is the cheap one; Terra exists. Beneath the joke is real info: Sol clearing a safety-eval compliance bar signals OpenAI's enterprise/regulatory positioning. The reach also shows "model naming is now like phone model numbers" has become an industry in-joke.
items.insightZh: Kothari 用一段爆火的「向老婆解释本周模型发布」段子把 GPT-5.6 三兄弟讲清楚了：Sol 是聪明的那个，发布前得先过政府安全评估——「像获得假释一样」；Luna 是便宜的那个；Terra 存在。玩笑之下是真信息：Sol 卡了安全 eval 的合规门槛，这是 OpenAI 面向企业/监管定位的信号。这条帖子的传播力（94 赞在他的量级里算高）也说明「模型命名越来越像手机型号」已经成了行业自嘲的梗。

items.title: Madhu Guru · Meta AI 高级总监（前 Google Gemini/Veo/Nano Banana）
items.summaryEn: A heavyweight talent move: Madhu Guru, who led Google Gemini, Veo, and Nano Banana, announced he's joining Meta to build AI products. His read is worth noting: while SWE agents have transformed software engineering, agents in most other complex systems are still early, and most people haven't felt the full power of AI agents yet — he sees Meta as well positioned to change that. It's both a career bet and a bet on where the next wave of agents lands: not in coding, but in other complex systems.
items.insightZh: 一条重量级人事流动：曾主导 Google Gemini、Veo、Nano Banana 的 Madhu Guru 官宣加入 Meta 做 AI 产品。他的判断值得记：虽然 SWE（软件工程）agent 已经彻底改变了软件开发，但在大多数其他复杂系统里，agent 还非常早期，多数人还没真正感受到 AI agent 的全部威力——他认为 Meta 正好卡在能改变这一点的位置上。这既是个人职业选择，也是对「agent 下一波在哪落地」的下注：不在写代码，在别的复杂系统。

items.title: Josh Woodward · Google Labs / Gemini App 副总裁
items.summaryEn: Woodward is doing a rare open product move: he stack-ranked the Top 10 user-requested features and gave status on each. He got 1,400+ replies in the first 12 hours and 300+ overnight, and says he read them all. Number one: make Google Workspace integrations actually work. This public "rank the feedback + report status per item" transparency is uncommon among big-tech product leads, and signals how the Gemini App team is playing for user trust.
items.insightZh: Woodward 在做一件难得的公开产品动作：他把用户反馈的 Top 10 需求做了 stack rank 并逐条给进度。首 12 小时收到 1,400+ 回复、隔夜又来 300+，他说全都读了。排第一的是「让 Google Workspace 集成真正好用」。这种「把用户反馈公开排序 + 逐项交代状态」的透明度在大厂产品负责人里不多见，是 Gemini App 团队在争夺用户信任上的姿态。

items.title: Garry Tan · Y Combinator CEO
items.summaryEn: Tan tested Meta Muse Spark 1.1 (early access codenamed Hornbill) and found it "really good" on his OpenClaw, congratulating Alexandr Wang by name. The value here is the signal — the head of YC publicly endorsing a new Meta model, in a hands-on agent environment (OpenClaw), corroborating Rauch's prediction that new models will grab share. Meta's presence in the model race is materially rebounding.
items.insightZh: Tan 亲测了 Meta Muse Spark 1.1（早期代号 Hornbill），结论是在他的 OpenClaw 上「真的很好」，点名恭喜 Alexandr Wang。这条的价值在于信号面——YC 掌门人公开为一个 Meta 新模型背书，且是在 agent 实操环境（OpenClaw）里，侧面印证了 Rauch「新模型将抢份额」的预判。Meta 在模型竞赛里的存在感正在实质性回升。

items.title: Swyx · Latent Space / Cognition
items.summaryEn: Swyx dropped a sharp AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) observation: no matter what transactional email infra he already has set up, all the leading frontier models keep trying to use Resend to send emails — he joked whoever does Resend's AEO deserves a raise. Behind it is a real question: as models become default recommendation engines, whoever gets "remembered" by models as the default tool for a task category wins a new distribution channel. AEO is becoming the next battleground after SEO.
items.insightZh: Swyx 抛了个 AEO（Answer Engine Optimization，「答案引擎优化」）的犀利观察：无论他已经配好了什么现成的事务性邮件基础设施，所有前沿模型都执着地想用 Resend 来发邮件——他调侃 Resend 做 AEO 的人该加薪。这背后是个真问题：当模型成为默认推荐引擎，谁被模型「记住」为某类任务的默认工具，谁就赢得了新的分发入口。AEO 正在成为继 SEO 之后的下一个兵家必争之地。
